transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
My sleep has been completely off for weeks now. Either I’m up most of the night with my mind going, or I crash and still wake up feeling completely worn out.

During the times when your mind is going and you sleep very little, do you also feel unusually energized or euphoric, more talkative, or like your thoughts are racing faster than usual? Have you had times like that lasting several days?

Yes, during those times I feel completely wired and on top of the world, and I'll stay up starting projects around the house because my mind is racing so fast. My husband says I talk a mile a minute, jumping from topic to topic, and these intense ups and downs have been happening on and off for about three months now.

During these “wired” periods, have you ever done things that got you into serious trouble, needed to be hospitalized, or felt so out of touch with reality that you believed things others said weren’t true? If yes, can you tell me whether that happened during the same period?

I haven't been hospitalized, but I've gotten written up at work for mistakes and there's been a lot of tension with my family. During those wired phases, I do feel out of touch because I'll hear a voice calling my name or whispering that I'm failing them, but that only ever happens when I'm in that high-energy state and stops completely when I crash.

During those high-energy periods when you hear the voice, do you also have times when you feel unusually powerful, chosen, or certain you can do things others say are impossible? Have these episodes ever made you unable to work or care for yourself for several days?

Yes, in those high-gear moments I feel like I have a special gift for seeing how everything fits together and that I'm the only one who can fix all our family and work problems. It has completely disrupted my life, though—I've been written up at the warehouse for mistakes, stopped going to church and volunteering, and my family has had to take over my usual responsibilities because they are tiptoeing around me.

opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes recurrent episodes over about three months of elevated/expansive mood, markedly decreased need for sleep, increased energy, pressured speech, racing thoughts, increased goal-directed activity, grandiose beliefs, and significant functional impairment. Psychotic symptoms (hearing whispers/voice calling name) occur only during the high-energy mood episodes, supporting a manic episode with psychotic symptoms within bipolar affective disorder rather than a primary psychotic disorder.
